caesar.help: Rotate the inner ring (drag, scroll wheel, or ← → keys) until the text becomes readable. Align the tallest ciphertext bar with the language's most frequent letter.
transposition.emptyTrace: Drag a path across the cells to build the text…
transposition.help: Drag the grid corner to change the column count (← → keys work too). When the grid becomes a perfect rectangle, you have found the dimensions. Now trace the route: snake, spiral, or column by column.
transposition.highlightHint: Click any letter to highlight every occurrence of it in the grid.
frequency.title: Frequency analysis
frequency.mapping.title: Substitution (cipher → plain)
frequency.palette.title: hypothesis (draft)
frequency.help: Click a letter and type a letter — a hypothesis. Enter — lock it, Backspace — clear, clicking the active letter again toggles lock. Right-click — quick palette.
frequency.ngramHelp: Drag across 2–3 letters — the system highlights every identical cluster in the text.
frequency.reference.title: Reference language frequencies
vigenere.help: Find repeated trigrams in the ciphertext (the Kasiski tab) — the distances between them are multiples of the key length. Then enter the key length and fit the shifts: every key position is its own Caesar cipher.
vigenere.kasiski.hint: Repeated sequences (3+ letters) and the distances between them.
vigenere.kasiski.highlighted: Found patterns are highlighted in the ciphertext (positions include spaces; distances are counted in letters).
vigenere.key.none: Enter the key length to open the shift sliders.
vigenere.decryption.empty: Enter the key length in the Key Fitting tab — the decrypted text will appear here.
